etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English enhauncen, anhaunsen, from Anglo-Norman anhauncer (“enhance, raise”), from Vulgar Latin *inaltiāre (“raise”), derived from Latin in + altus (“high”). The /h/ in Old French was taken from haut (“high”), where it resulted from Frankish influence.

quote.citation: 1590, Edmund Spenser, “Book I, Canto I”, in The Faerie Queene. […], London:  […]  [John Wolfe] for William Ponsonbie, →OCLC:
quote.text: nought aghast, his mightie hand enhaunst: / The stroke down from her head vnto her shoulder glaunst.

definitions.definition: To augment or make something greater.

quote.citation: 1831, Robert Southey, Sir Thomas More: Or Colloquies on the Progress and Prospects of Society, page 214:
quote.text: They had no character to preserve, except for courage; and perhaps the reputation of ferocity enhanced the value of their services, in making them feared as well as hated by the people.

quote.citation: 2000, Mordecai Roshwald, Liberty: Its Meaning and Scope, page 155:
quote.text: A hereditary monarch relies on pomp and ceremony, which enhance the respect for the institution

definitions.definition: To improve something by adding features.

quote.citation: 1986, Maggie Righetti, Knitting in Plain English, page 192:
quote.text: A pom-pom to top off a stocking cap, a fringe to feather the edge of a shawl, tassels to define the points of an afghan, these are just a few of the delightful little goodies that enhance handknit things.

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To be raised up; to grow larger.
(radiology) To take up contrast agent (for an organ, tissue, or lesion).
